the 50–66 GHz DPLL has a phase noise of −94.5 dBc/Hz, a fractional spur of −52 dBc, and a jitter of 220 fs.

the 50-66-GHz DPLL achieves a 10-dB phase noise improvement over a state-of-the-art analog PLL, and a 10-dBC improvement over a 60-GHz fractional-N PLL.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a phase-domain DPLL with a fundamental frequency DCO is capable of synthesizing a 50– 66-GHz signal with low jitter and low fractional spurs, and that the DCO nonlinearity can be mitigated by digital calibration.
DPLLs are feasible at mm-wave frequencies and offer the potential for low power and low cost, especially in view of the fact that our prototype is implemented in a standard CMOS process.

digital phase-domain PLLs can be used for mm-wave frequency synthesis, with the potential to achieve better jitter performance, lower phase noise and lower fractional spurs than analog sub-harmonic PLLs, while occupying less chip area and consuming lower supply current.
